items.author: mel_k
items.title: Achilles sore after upping my k's - rest or push on?
items.body: Hi all, been building for the Rottnest half in Feb. Went from about 30km a week to 48 in the space of three weeks (I know, I know). Right Achilles is stiff as anything first thing in the morning, sore to squeeze about 3-4cm up from the heel, eases off after 10 min of running then aches that night. Bit of a lump there too. No pop or anything sudden. Do I stop completely? Keep going slower? Someone at work said do heel drops off a step, how many and how often? Cheers

items.author: GazzaRunsWA
items.body: Had the same in 2019. Stretch it hard morning and night, lean on the wall till it burns. If it's still bad go see a GP and get a cortisone shot, sorted mine in a week.

items.author: trailgirl_lou
items.body: I just put a heel lift in my shoes and ran through it. Took ages to go though. Maybe @kaz_physio can chime in, Kaz knows this stuff

items.author: mel_k
items.body: Thanks guys. Did a 6k this morning, felt ok while running but limping around the office after. Physio would be great if anyone has thoughts, I'm in Bayswater if that matters. Not keen on a needle if I can avoid it

items.author: runner_pete
items.title: Outside of knee pain on downhills
items.body: Getting a sharp pain on the outside of my left knee after about 8km, worse on the downhills at Kings Park. Foam rolling not doing much. Anyone had ITB issues?

items.author: kaz_physio
items.body: Pete foam rolling the ITB itself won't change much, it's not a muscle you can stretch out. Usually it's a load thing. Cut back the downhills for a couple of weeks, work on your glutes and hip strength, side-lying leg raises and single leg squats in front of a mirror. If it's not settling in 3 weeks get it looked at properly.

items.author: bev.h
items.title: DM: bev.h
items.body: Hi Kaz, saw Mel's thread. Just between us, mine went (full rupture) the winter after I was on ciprofloxacin for a nasty UTI, the surgeon reckoned that was half of it. I've never told the club and I'd rather not have it out there, but if you think it's worth a general warning about antibiotics go for it, just please don't mention me or the details. Bev
